Growth doesn't begin with strength.
It begins with honesty—the moment you
finally exhale and whisper,
'God... I don't know how to keep going.'
welcome.description:
A quiet invitation to pause, to breathe,
and to let Him meet you in your own quiet place.

brainGames.title: Brain Games
brainGames.subtitle: Evidence-based exercises for emotional wellness
brainGames.unlockDescription: 6 evidence-based exercises designed to rewire your brain for peace and resilience.
brainGames.potterVerse: "The potter formed it into another pot, shaping it as seemed best to him."
brainGames.disclaimer: FOR EDUCATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. These exercises are wellness tools based on general scientific principles. They are NOT therapy or professional mental health treatment. The creators are not medical professionals. If you're in crisis, please seek professional help immediately.

prompts.comfortTaken: What's a comfort you often take for granted?
prompts.prayerAnswered: What's a prayer that was answered?
prompts.madeSmile: What made you smile this week?

encouragements.lovelySeed: What a lovely seed of gratitude.

thoughtDetective.whatThinking: What negative thought keeps coming back?
thoughtDetective.captureSubtitle: What's bothering you? Write it exactly as it appears in your mind.
thoughtDetective.captureHint: Be honest and specific. This is completely private.
thoughtDetective.identifySubtitle: Which thinking trap might this be?
thoughtDetective.investigateSubtitle: Let's examine this thought more closely
thoughtDetective.reframeSubtitle: Write a kinder version of this thought
thoughtDetective.encouragement: Every time you reframe a thought, you're rewiring your brain for healthier thinking patterns.

allOrNothing.name: All-or-Nothing Thinking
allOrNothing.description: Seeing things in black and white, with no middle ground.
allOrNothing.example: "If I can't do it perfectly, I shouldn't do it at all"
allOrNothing.reframePrompt: What's a more balanced way to see this? Is there any gray area?
allOrNothing.selfCompassionPrompt: What would you say to a friend who made the same mistake?
allOrNothing.scripture: "His mercies are new every morning." - Lamentations 3:23

alwaysNever.name: Always/Never Thinking
alwaysNever.example: "You never listen to me" or "I always mess things up"
alwaysNever.reframePrompt: Is this really always or never? Can you think of one exception?
alwaysNever.selfCompassionPrompt: We all struggle sometimes. What's actually true most of the time?
alwaysNever.scripture: "Weeping may endure for a night, but joy comes in the morning." - Psalm 30:5

focusingNegative.name: Focusing on the Negative
focusingNegative.description: Only seeing the bad while ignoring the good.
focusingNegative.example: Getting 9 compliments and 1 criticism, but only remembering the criticism
focusingNegative.reframePrompt: What good things are you overlooking? What went well?
focusingNegative.selfCompassionPrompt: Your brain is wired to notice threats. What would a balanced view look like?
focusingNegative.scripture: "Whatever is true, noble, right, pure, lovely... think about such things." - Philippians 4:8

fortuneTelling.name: Fortune Telling
fortuneTelling.description: Predicting the future negatively without evidence.
fortuneTelling.example: "I know this won't work out" or "They're going to reject me"
fortuneTelling.reframePrompt: Is this prediction based on facts or fears? What evidence do you have?
fortuneTelling.selfCompassionPrompt: Uncertainty is hard. What if you stayed open to positive possibilities?
fortuneTelling.scripture: "For I know the plans I have for you... plans to give you hope and a future." - Jeremiah 29:11

mindReading.name: Mind Reading
mindReading.description: Assuming you know what others are thinking.
mindReading.example: "They think I'm stupid" or "She doesn't like me"
mindReading.reframePrompt: What do you actually know for certain? Could there be another explanation?
mindReading.selfCompassionPrompt: We can't read minds. What would you need to feel more secure?
mindReading.scripture: "Man looks at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart." - 1 Samuel 16:7

thinkingWithFeelings.name: Thinking with Feelings
thinkingWithFeelings.description: Believing something is true just because you feel it.
thinkingWithFeelings.example: "I feel like a burden, so I must be one"
thinkingWithFeelings.reframePrompt: Just because you feel it, does that make it true? What are the facts?
thinkingWithFeelings.selfCompassionPrompt: Feelings are real but they're not always accurate. What's actually true?
thinkingWithFeelings.scripture: "The heart is deceitful above all things." - Jeremiah 17:9

guiltBeating.name: Guilt Beating
guiltBeating.description: Using "should" or "must" to beat yourself up.
guiltBeating.example: "I should be over this by now" or "I ought to be stronger"
guiltBeating.reframePrompt: What if you replaced "should" with "I would like to"?
guiltBeating.selfCompassionPrompt: You're being hard on yourself. What do you actually need right now?
guiltBeating.scripture: "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness." - 2 Corinthians 12:9

labeling.name: Labeling
labeling.description: Attaching a negative label instead of describing behavior.
labeling.example: "I'm a failure" instead of "I made a mistake"
labeling.reframePrompt: Would you say this to a friend? What's a kinder description?
labeling.selfCompassionPrompt: You are not your worst moment. Who are you beyond this label?
labeling.scripture: "You are fearfully and wonderfully made." - Psalm 139:14

blame.name: Blame
blame.description: Blaming others or yourself for things outside your control.
blame.example: "It's all my fault" or "You make me feel..."
blame.reframePrompt: What parts were in your control? What parts were not?
blame.selfCompassionPrompt: Taking responsibility is different from taking blame.
blame.scripture: "Cast your burden on the Lord, and He shall sustain you." - Psalm 55:22

scripturePalace.welcomeText: The Method of Loci is an ancient memory technique. Place scriptures in rooms of your mental palace, and associate each with a vivid image. When you revisit the rooms, the scriptures will return to you.
scripturePalace.tapRoomHint: Tap a room to place or review a scripture
scripturePalace.scripture: "I have hidden your word in my heart that I might not sin against you."
scripturePalace.tourSubtitle: You walked through your memory palace
scripturePalace.encouragement: Each visit strengthens your memory. God's word is taking root in your heart.

entrance.name: Entrance Hall
entrance.visualScene: Imagine standing at a grand wooden door. Warm golden light spills through. As you enter, you see this scripture carved into the stone archway above.
entrance.memoryTip: Picture the words glowing on the entrance stone

garden.name: Garden of Eden
garden.description: A place of peace and creation
garden.visualScene: You step into a lush garden with blooming flowers and a gentle stream. Butterflies dance around as you read these words on an ancient garden stone.
garden.memoryTip: See the words growing like vines on the stone

living.name: Living Room
living.visualScene: A cozy room with a crackling fireplace. Soft cushions invite you to sit. Above the mantle, these words are painted in elegant script.
living.memoryTip: Feel the warmth of the fire as you read

kitchen.name: Bread of Life Kitchen
kitchen.visualScene: The aroma of fresh bread fills the air. A wooden table holds a feast. On the wall, written in flour-dusted chalk, you see these words.
kitchen.memoryTip: Smell the bread as you memorize

study.name: Wisdom Study
study.visualScene: Floor-to-ceiling bookshelves surround you. A lamp illuminates an open book on the desk. These words are highlighted on the page.
study.memoryTip: Hear the pages rustling as you learn

bedroom.name: Rest Chamber
bedroom.visualScene: Moonlight streams through gauze curtains. A peaceful bed awaits. On the pillow, embroidered in silver thread, you see these words.
bedroom.memoryTip: Feel the peace wash over you

tower.name: Watchtower
tower.visualScene: You climb spiral stairs to the top. The view stretches to the horizon. Carved into the tower wall, catching the sunlight, are these words.
tower.memoryTip: See the vast view as you remember

throne.name: Throne Room
throne.visualScene: Golden light fills a majestic hall. A throne of pure light sits ahead. On the floor before it, written in gold, are these words.
throne.memoryTip: Feel the majesty as you bow

intro.title: Release What You Carry
intro.description: Our bodies store emotions and tension, often without us realizing. This gentle scan will help you notice where you're holding stress and guide you to release it with compassion.
intro.scripture: "Come to me, all who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest."

head.name: Head
head.instruction: Bring attention to your head. Notice any tension in your forehead, temples, or jaw.
head.releasePrompt: With each exhale, let the tension dissolve. Imagine a warm, golden light softening every muscle.
head.scripture: "He gives peace to your borders." - Psalm 147:14

neck.name: Neck
neck.instruction: Move your attention to your neck and throat. This area often holds unspoken words and tension.
neck.releasePrompt: Gently roll your head if it helps. Release any tightness with gratitude for your voice.
neck.scripture: "Let the words of my mouth be acceptable." - Psalm 19:14

shoulders.name: Shoulders
shoulders.instruction: Feel into your shoulders. This is where we carry burdens and responsibilities.
shoulders.releasePrompt: Let your shoulders drop. You don't have to carry everything alone.
shoulders.scripture: "Cast your burden on the Lord." - Psalm 55:22

chest.name: Chest
chest.instruction: Bring awareness to your chest and heart space. Notice your breath rising and falling.
chest.releasePrompt: Place a hand on your heart if you wish. You are safe. You are held.

stomach.name: Stomach
stomach.instruction: Notice your belly. This area often holds anxiety and "gut feelings."
stomach.releasePrompt: Breathe deeply into your belly. Let it soften completely with each breath.
stomach.scripture: "Do not be anxious about anything." - Philippians 4:6

back.name: Back
back.instruction: Scan your lower back. This region supports you and often holds stress.
back.releasePrompt: Imagine warmth spreading through your lower back, releasing all tension.

hands.name: Hands
hands.instruction: Feel your arms and hands. Are they clenched or relaxed?
hands.releasePrompt: Open your palms. Release anything you've been holding onto too tightly.
hands.scripture: "I will hold your right hand." - Isaiah 41:13

legs.name: Legs
legs.instruction: Bring attention to your thighs and legs. They carry you through each day.
legs.releasePrompt: Let your legs feel heavy and grounded. You are supported.
legs.scripture: "He makes my feet like the feet of a deer." - Psalm 18:33

feet.name: Feet
feet.instruction: Finally, notice your feet. Feel them grounded to the earth.
feet.releasePrompt: Imagine roots growing from your feet, connecting you to stability and peace.
feet.scripture: "How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news." - Romans 10:15

tensionQuestion.before: How much tension do you feel here?

complete.title: Scan Complete
complete.subtitle: You've journeyed through your body with awareness

sessionComplete.title: Body Scan Complete

patternPeace.title: Pattern Peace
patternPeace.subtitle: N-Back Working Memory Training

intro.description: Train your working memory through focused attention. This exercise helps quiet ruminating thoughts by engaging your mind in purposeful pattern recognition.

instructions.watchGridDesc: A symbol will appear in one of the 9 squares.
instructions.rememberDesc1: Compare the current stimulus to the previous one.
instructions.rememberDescN: Compare the current stimulus to {{nBack}} stimuli ago.
instructions.matchPositionDesc: Press "Position Match" if the square is the same as {{nBack}} ago.
instructions.matchSymbolDesc: Press "Symbol Match" if the symbol is the same as {{nBack}} ago.
instructions.tip: Both matches can happen at once! If position AND symbol match, press both buttons.

patternPeace.quickInstruction1: Tap if position OR symbol matches the previous one
patternPeace.quickInstructionN: Tap if position OR symbol matches {{nBack}} ago

completeMessages.excellent: Excellent focus! Your working memory is getting stronger.
completeMessages.good: Good effort! Consistent practice brings lasting peace.
completeMessages.keepPracticing: Keep practicing. Each session trains your mind for stillness.

scriptures.isaiah26: "You will keep in perfect peace those whose minds are steadfast." - Isaiah 26:3
scriptures.peter5: "Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you." - 1 Peter 5:7
scriptures.psalm29: "The Lord gives strength to his people; the Lord blesses his people with peace." - Psalm 29:11

encouragements.peaceful: Your mind is becoming more peaceful.
encouragements.stillness: You are training your mind for stillness.
encouragements.gift: Every moment of focus is a gift to yourself.

disclaimer.title: Educational Exercise
disclaimer.content: Pattern Peace is a cognitive training exercise based on N-back research. It is educational in nature and is not a substitute for professional mental health treatment. If you're experiencing persistent cognitive difficulties, please consult a healthcare provider.
